funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland

records.justification: The agent's text supports claims about the grant covering tuition fees, being for low-income students in Scotland who cannot get government fee support, but omits the claim about the grant being offered since 1901.

claims.text: The grant covers undergraduate tuition fees.
The grant is for low-income students.
The grant is for students in Scotland.
The grant is for students who cannot get government fee support.
The grant has been offered since 1901.

records.justification: All claims made in the agent's text are directly supported by the provided page text, covering aspects of eligibility, funding amounts, application deadlines, and the application process.

claims.text: Grants cover tuition fees for individuals from low-income households.
Grants are for individuals who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government.
Grants are for individuals studying for a first degree.
Grants are for individuals studying for a second degree in limited cases.
Grants are for individuals studying at a Scottish higher education institution.
The grants cover tuition fees up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.
Applicants must demonstrate that their financial circumstances do not allow them to cover the cost of their tuition fees.
Retrospective applications will not be accepted.
Applications will not be accepted if the student has incurred tuition fee debts in a previous year of study and is unable to move to the next level of their course as a result.
Applicants must live in a low-income household.

Applicants must be ordinarily resident in Scotland at the time of applying and have completed at least two full years of secondary schooling or college education in Scotland, OR be able to demonstrate a substantial and recent connection to Scotland.
Applicants must be entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain under a visa valid for the entire duration of the course, or be an asylum seeker.
Applicants must not be eligible for public funds (e.g. grants or loans) towards the cost of tuition fees.
Applicants must not have already graduated with a university degree.
Applications from students who already have a university degree qualification may be considered exceptionally at the discretion of CEF for a second undergraduate degree.
The application portal will be open from June 1, 2026, to 5 pm on December 1, 2026, for grants covering academic year 2026-27.
Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis.
The awards cover tuition fees only, up to a maximum of £1,820.
The grants are designed to help students who do not have the financial resources to attend university.
The total household gross income thresholds are used as guides when assessing applications.
Applications are reviewed holistically with an applicant’s personal as well as financial circumstances considered.
The student living cost loan or any social benefits are not regarded as forming part of an applicant’s total household income.
Applications are considered on a case-by-case basis.
CEF may request additional supporting evidence.
All applications are made online.
An eligibility checker must be completed before applying.
The application form is only accessible during the application window.

Late applications after the closing date will not be accepted, unless the student can demonstrate that they were first informed that SAAS would not be covering their fees after CEF’s online portal has closed.
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their applications within two to three weeks, provided all requested information and a timely referee response are submitted.
A decision will be communicated via email to the address listed on the application form.
Supporting documents include evidence of applicant eligibility, a letter of acceptance for the university course, SAAS Award Notice letter, and P60 or pay slips/Universal Credit statements.
Students receiving a SAAS bursary must provide a copy of their SAAS award letter.
Supporting evidence can be submitted as scanned copies or mobile images.
There is a 5MB size limit on each file submitted online.

Funding is capped at a maximum of £5,000 per year.
